title: A `@check` can claim paths with `check.covers`; `check.scope` stays text and claims none
summary: Plan amendments C17 and C22. compliance-system's `@check` schema gains an optional check.covers, a list of text path selections, and documents check.scope, still required text, as what the check selects (the whole-workspace token *, a scope its evaluator reports, or prose). @inventarch/graph adds check.covers to CLAIM_FIELDS, so the claimant index, claimants(graph, path), db resolveSeat's claimants, db inertDeclarations, ia position's location seats and every other reader of claimants name a check whose covers selects a path, with field check.covers; a check's check.scope is still never a claim, even text that reads as a path, and claiming a path changes nothing about which verdicts ia validate binds the check to. A workspace that states no check.covers sees no change apart from its revision, which moves with the new schema bytes. The public vocabulary (docs/reference/language/vocabulary.json and .md, the CLI and door catalogues), the generated authoring reference for `@check` (shipped in @inventarch/authoring-system) and the authoring resource manifest are regenerated, and @inventarch/compliance-system ships the new schema, and the bundled inventarch/language base and the embedded host payload are rebuilt from the new schema, which moves the host payload pin. The coordinated native transition selects 2.1.0 for all twelve native archives, including inventarch/language, compliance-system and authoring-system. The native release ledger and gate preserve published id@version bytes and require content-driven version selection against the immutable published baseline; this release does not replace the published 1.2.0 bytes. Native versions remain independent from the npm cohort. Admission follows the schema bytes a workspace has installed, not the CLI reading it: a workspace still on the 2.0.0 base (inventarch/language 1.2.0 with the old bytes) cannot state check.covers, under any CLI, until its base moves, and a reader older than this release admits the field where the workspace's base declares it but does not treat it as a claim.
